# FDG9073

> DO NOT make public types finalizable.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.4.2 Finalizable Types.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9073
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Move the finalizer of the public type '{0}' to an internal or private nested resource holder

Library only: the text is about public types, and moves the finalizer to an internal or private nested type. FDG9073 reports a finalizer declared in an externally visible class. A public type that inherits a finalizer, such as a public subclass of SafeHandle, is not reported, so coverage is partial. Removing an override of Finalize changes no public signature, so autofix is no; there is no code fix. On a type that already shipped with a finalizer, FDG9077 asks to keep it. CA2216 (disposable types should declare a finalizer) asks for the opposite and is not mapped.

## From the book

Public types that hold finalizable resources should instead make an internal, or private nested, type to be a finalizable resource holder. Prefer using existing resource wrappers, such as `SafeHandle`, to encapsulate unmanaged resources where possible.

```csharp
// wrong
public partial class NetworkCard : IDisposable {
  private IntPtr _deviceHandle;

  ~NetworkCard() {
    Dispose(false);
  }

  public bool Dispose() => Dispose(true);

  protected bool Dispose(bool disposing) {
    if (_deviceHandle != IntPtr.Zero) {
      Interop.CloseHandle(_deviceHandle);
      _deviceHandle = IntPtr.Zero;
    }
  }
}

// right
public partial class NetworkCard : IDisposable {
  private SafeDeviceHandle _deviceHandle;

  public bool Dispose() => Dispose(true);
  protected bool Dispose(bool disposing) {
    if (disposing) {
      _deviceHandle?.Dispose();
    }
  }
}
internal sealed class SafeDeviceHandle :
  SaveHandleZeroOrMinusOneIsInvalid {

  internal SafeDeviceHandle()
    : base(ownsHandle: true)
  {
  }
  protected override bool ReleaseHandle() {
    return Interop.CloseHandle(_handle);
  }
}
```
